stem: Which of the following is an example of an active digital footprint?
options: Cookies stored when a website is visited
The IP address logged by a web server
A comment posted on a friend's blog
The location recorded by a mobile app
explanation: Correct option: (C). An active digital footprint is data we submit intentionally, such as a comment we choose to post. Cookies, an IP address logged by a server and location recorded by an app are generated without us deliberately submitting them, so they are passive footprints.

stem: Riya deletes an old photo she had posted on a social networking site and clears her browser history. Which statement about her digital footprint is correct?
options: It is fully erased because the post and history are gone
Copies may still remain on the servers hosting the site
It is erased once the browser cookies are also cleared
Only active footprints remain, never the passive ones
explanation: Correct option: (B). Most digital footprints are stored on the servers where applications are hosted, and the user has no control over removing them, so there is no guarantee they are fully eliminated. Deleting the post, history or cookies only removes local or visible copies, and passive data such as server logs can also remain.
